headline: Cypriot natural gas could start flowing from ExxonMobil's discoveries by 2033
summary: Natural gas could start flowing by 2033 out of two undersea deposits discovered by ExxonMobil off Cyprus, a senior executive with the company said Tuesday, helping to turn the east Mediterranean island nation into a new European energy hub.  The largest U.S. oil company and its consortium partner, QatarEnergy, consider the most likely option for getting the gas to market would be conveying it through a pipeline to existing processing facilities in Egypt where it can be liquefied for export, ExxonMobil's Vice President of Global Exploration John Ardill said.  Other options including building onshore facilities in Cyprus or a floating one in waters over the deposits are considered too costly at this point.
